CHAPTER.VERS:
O that thou as my brother, that was nourished at the breasts of my mother! I should find thee outside, I would kiss thee; yea, I should not be despised.
I should not…: Heb. they should not despise me
I would lead thee, bring thee into my mother’s house, would instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate.
His left hand under my head, and his right hand should embrace me.

I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not, nor awake love, until he please.
that…: Heb. why should ye stir up, or, why, etc
Who this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I awakened thee under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth: there she brought thee forth bore thee.

Set me as a seal upon thy heart, as a seal upon thy arm: for love strong as death; jealousy cruel as the grave: the coals of it coals of fire, most vehement flame.
cruel: Heb. hard
Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be despised.
We have a little sister, and she hath no breasts: what shall we do for our sister in the day when she shall be spoken for?
If she a wall, we will build upon her a palace of silver: and if she a door, we will inclose her with boards of cedar.

I a wall, and my breasts like towers: then was I in his eyes as one that found favour.
favour: Heb. peace
Solomon had a vineyard at Baalhamon; he let out the vineyard to keepers; every one for the fruit of it was to bring a thousand of silver.
My vineyard, which mine, before me: thou, O Solomon, a thousand, and those that keep the fruit of it two hundred.
Thou that dwellest in the gardens, the companions hearken to thy voice: cause me to hear .

Make haste, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of spices.
Make…: Heb. Flee away
